D: Two Miami narcotics detectives swap identities to protect a witness.
P: Serve dinner when Marcus has to pretend to be Mike.
S: Thick béchamel with finely chopped ham and nutmeg, chilled overnight, rolled into logs, egg and crumb, fried at 180C until golden.
South Beach prawn fritters with lime mayo

Chopped prawns in a light batter with capsicum, onion, celery and chilli, fried in spoonfuls until crisp, with a zesty lime and chilli mayo. Finely chop 400g peeled green prawns. Whisk 150g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 1 egg and 125ml milk into a thick batter. Fold in the prawns, half a finely diced red capsicum, half a diced onion, 1 diced celery stick, 1 chopped chilli and salt. Drop tablespoons into oil at 180C and fry 3 minutes until golden. Mix 120g mayo with the zest and juice of 1 lime and a pinch of cayenne.
Very ripe plantains sliced on the bias, fried in oil at medium heat until caramelised and soft, flaky salt.
M: Cuban bread (or a soft long roll) with mustard, mojo pork, leg ham, Swiss and pickles, buttered and pressed until crisp and flat.
Miami jerk chicken with rice and peas

Chicken thighs marinated overnight in scotch bonnet, allspice, thyme, garlic and lime, grilled slowly until charred, with coconut rice and kidney beans. Blend 4 spring onions, 1 scotch bonnet, 3 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp allspice, 1 tbsp thyme leaves, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp brown sugar and the juice of 2 limes. Coat 1kg chicken thighs and marinate overnight. Grill over medium heat for 20 to 25 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through. Simmer 300g rice with a 400ml tin coconut milk, 200ml water, a drained 400g tin kidney beans and a thyme sprig, covered, for 18 minutes.
W: Biscuit crust baked 10 minutes. Whisk 400g condensed milk, 4 yolks and 120ml lime juice with zest, bake at 160C for 15 minutes, chill, whipped cream.
K: Mike's apartment with the ocean view
Mint muddled gently with sugar syrup and lime, white rum and crushed ice, topped with soda.

edition.cue: Serve dinner when Marcus has to pretend to be Mike.

s.note: Crisp crumbed ham croquettes with thick béchamel and a little nutmeg.
s.how: Melt 30g butter, stir in 40g plain flour and cook 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in 250ml full cream milk and cook 5 minutes until a very thick béchamel forms. Stir in 120g finely chopped leg ham and 1/8 tsp nutmeg. Spread in a shallow dish, cool promptly and refrigerate overnight. Shape into 8 logs. Dust with 20g flour, dip in 1 beaten egg and coat in 60g breadcrumbs. Fry in neutral oil at 180°C for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and hot throughout. Drain and serve two each.

s.note: Caramelised ripe plantain slices, soft inside with a flaky salt finish.
s.how: Peel 2 very ripe plantains and cut diagonally into 1cm slices. Heat 3 tbsp vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Fry the slices in batches for 3 minutes each side until caramelised and soft. Drain and finish with 1/4 tsp sea salt flakes.

m.note: Pressed bread with mojo pork, ham, Swiss, mustard and pickles.
m.how: Marinate 700g boneless pork shoulder overnight with juice of 1 orange and 1 lime, 3 crushed garlic cloves, 1 tsp oregano, 1 tsp cumin and 1/2 tsp salt. Put in a covered roasting dish with 100ml water and roast at 160°C conventional for about 3 hours until tender; rest 20 minutes and shred. Split 4 long soft rolls and spread with 40g yellow mustard. Fill with the pork, 120g leg ham, 120g Swiss cheese and 80g sliced dill pickles. Butter the outsides with 30g butter and press in a hot sandwich press for 5 minutes, until crisp and flat and the filling is piping hot.

w.note: Biscuit crust, lime custard and a cool whipped cream topping.
w.how: Crush 150g digestive biscuits, mix with 60g melted butter and press into a 20cm pie dish. Bake at 180°C conventional for 10 minutes. Whisk 400g condensed milk with 4 egg yolks, 120ml lime juice and zest of 2 limes. Pour into the crust and bake at 160°C for 15 minutes until just set. Cool and refrigerate for at least 4 hours. Softly whip 100ml thickened cream and spread over the pie. Cut four generous portions.

d.note: Mint, lime, white rum and soda over plenty of crushed ice.
d.how: Gently muddle 24 mint leaves with 60ml sugar syrup and 60ml lime juice in a jug, avoiding shredding the mint. Add 180ml white rum. Divide between four glasses filled with 500g crushed ice. Top with 400ml soda water and stir gently. Garnish with 4 mint sprigs.
